description: Teach-mode + passive coaching during history. Educational only.

modules.title: Dyspnoea history structure
points: Distinguish acute vs chronic, and exertional vs at-rest vs orthopnoea/PND — this separates cardiac from pulmonary patterns.
Always screen chest pain, leg swelling, and mental status alongside breathlessness.
In a GI context, ascites/hepatic hydrothorax and severe anaemia are important non-cardiopulmonary causes to keep on the list.

modules.title: Dyspnoea red flags
points: Reduced air entry, hypotension, or marked tachypnoea alongside dyspnoea warrant urgent escalation.
Do not delay oxygen/monitoring to finish the chronic history.

Q000070.why_ask: Positional pattern (rest vs exertion vs orthopnoea/PND) is a core cardiac-vs-pulmonary discriminator.
Q000070.think: Orthopnoea/PND point toward a cardiac or fluid-overload mechanism.

Q000072.why_ask: Leg swelling alongside dyspnoea suggests a fluid-overload or right-heart process.
Q000072.think: Unilateral swelling instead raises DVT/PE concern rather than heart failure.

answer_triggers.title: Unlocked: orthopnoea/PND pattern
points: Ask about leg swelling and recent weight gain.
